title: Constructing a gnotobiotic mouse model with a synthetic human gut microbiome
author: Steimle, De Sciscio, et al.

steps.title: Set up anaerobic chamber
steps.instruction: Place the anaerobic chamber at 37 °C with an atmosphere of 85 % N₂, 10 % CO₂ and 5 % H₂, using a palladium catalyst; put all culture media and plasticware inside the chamber at least 24 h before use to allow oxygen reduction.

steps.title: Prepare basic component powder
steps.instruction: Make 30 aliquots (2.31 g each) of the mYCFA basic component powder for 3 L of medium (total 69.7 g).

substeps.instruction: In a 1 L beaker combine the components listed in Table 2 (Casitone/Peptone, Yeast extract, NaHCO₃, Cysteine, K₂HPO₄, NaCl, MgSO₄·7H₂O, CaCl₂, Resazurin, Hemin) to obtain a homogeneous powder.
Mix thoroughly with a ~20 cm metal or plastic stick, then homogenize in 10 g batches using a mortar until the powder is fine‑grained.
Aliquot 2.31 g of the fine powder into 50 mL screw‑cap tubes and store at 4 °C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Prepare SCFA mix
steps.instruction: Prepare 30 aliquots (287 µL each) of the short‑chain fatty acid (SCFA) mix for 3 L of medium (total 8.607 mL).

substeps.instruction: Under a fume hood, add the acids listed in Table 3 (acetic, propionic, isobutyric, isovaleric, valeric) to a vessel to obtain 8.607 mL total volume.
Vortex the mixture, filter‑sterilize through a 0.22 µm filter, and aliquot 287 µL into sterile 1.5 mL screw‑cap tubes.
Seal the tubes with parafilm and store at 4 °C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Prepare vitamin mix
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL of the mYCFA vitamin mix (sufficient for 1 000 × 100 µL aliquots).

substeps.instruction: Add the vitamins listed in Table 4 (Biotin, Vitamin B12, 4‑aminobenzoic acid, Folic acid, Pyridoxine HCl, Thiamine HCl, Riboflavin) to a 200 mL glass bottle.
Resuspend in 100 mL ddH₂O, vortex, and filter‑sterilize through a 0.22 µm filter.
Aliquot 100 µL into sterile, light‑protected 1.5 mL tubes; store at 4 °C in the dark for up to 6 months. Keep the remaining bulk solution covered with aluminum foil at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare glucose solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 3 g glucose in 15 mL ddH₂O (200 mg mL⁻¹), filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm) and aliquot 500 µL into sterile 1.5 mL tubes; store at –20 °C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Prepare N‑acetyl‑D‑glucosamine solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 3 g N‑acetyl‑D‑glucosamine in 15 mL ddH₂O (200 mg mL⁻¹), filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm) and aliquot 500 µL into sterile 1.5 mL tubes; store at –20 °C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Prepare Buffer A for DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL Buffer A (1 × 10⁻¹ M NaCl, 0.2 M Trizma Base, 0.02 M EDTA pH 8.0).

substeps.instruction: Add 1.169 g NaCl, 2.423 g Trizma Base and 4 mL 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) to a 200 mL glass bottle.
Fill to 100 mL with ddH₂O, filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm), and store at room temperature (20‑25 °C) for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Prepare 3 M sodium acetate solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 mL of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2).

substeps.instruction: Resuspend 4.08 g sodium acetate in 8 mL ddH₂O.
Adjust pH to 5.2, then bring the volume to 10 mL with ddH₂O.
Filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm) and store at room temperature for up to 6 months.
Resuspend 4.0 g sodium dodecyl sulfate in 15 mL ddH₂O.
Filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm) and store at room temperature for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Assemble complete mYCFA medium
steps.instruction: Generate 100 mL of ready‑to‑use mYCFA medium (color changes indicate progress).

substeps.instruction: Dissolve one 2.31 g aliquot of the basic component powder in 50 mL ddH₂O (solution turns blue).
Transfer the 50 mL to a 200 mL glass bottle, rinse the original tube with an additional 50 mL ddH₂O and add the rinse to reach 100 mL total.
Add one 287 µL aliquot of the SCFA mix (solution turns purple and bubbles).
Add one 100 µL aliquot of the vitamin mix.
Add one 500 µL aliquot of the glucose solution.
Add one 500 µL aliquot of the N‑acetyl‑D‑glucosamine solution.
Add 444 µL of 60 % sodium lactate solution.
Adjust the pH to 6.8 (solution turns pink).
Filter‑sterilize the complete medium (0.22 µm).
Transfer the filtered medium into the anaerobic chamber, leave the screw cap slightly loosened, and incubate for at least 24 h for oxygen reduction (color changes to yellow).
After the color turns yellow, tighten the cap; use the medium within 72 h.

steps.title: Reduce oxygen in mYCFA medium
steps.instruction: Leave the freshly prepared mYCFA medium in the anaerobic chamber for a minimum of 24 h with the cap loosely closed; when the color changes from pink to yellow, the medium is oxygen‑reduced and ready for use (must be used within 72 h).

steps.title: Culture bacterial strains (timeline)
steps.instruction: Grow the 14 human gut commensals in mYCFA medium according to the following schedule:

substeps.instruction: Day 1: Inoculate each strain separately in mYCFA medium.
Day 2: Dilute each overnight culture once.
Day 3: Dilute each culture a second time.
Day 4: Mix the 14 diluted cultures to create the bacterial suspension for the first intragastric gavage (first of two consecutive gavages).
Day 5: Further dilute the remaining cultures and perform the second gavage.
Day 9 (5 days after the first gavage): Collect fecal samples for DNA isolation and colonization verification.

steps.title: Perform qPCR linear regression
steps.instruction: For each strain‑specific primer pair, generate a standard curve and calculate DNA concentrations from Cq values.

substeps.instruction: Plot the detected Cq of each pure‑culture standard against the logarithm of its known DNA concentration and fit a linear regression (example equation: y = ‑4.29 × x + 19.052).
Record the linear function for each primer pair.

steps.title: Calculate DNA concentrations and relative abundances
steps.instruction: Derive strain‑specific DNA amounts in fecal samples and compute their relative abundances.

substeps.instruction: Insert the sample Cq into the corresponding regression equation to obtain log[DNA]; e.g., for Cq = 17.93, log[DNA] = (17.93‑19.052)/‑4.29 = 0.261.
Convert log[DNA] to concentration: [DNA] = 10^0.261 ≈ 1.82 ng µL⁻¹.
Since 1 µL of isolated DNA was used per qPCR, the starting quantity (QS) equals 1.82 ng.
Repeat the calculation for every strain, then sum all QS values to obtain the total bacterial DNA quantity (QT); example total QT = 23.489 ng.
Compute the relative abundance of each strain: rel ab = (QS / QT) × 100 %; e.g., for Akkermansia muciniphila, rel ab = 1.82 / 23.489 × 100 ≈ 7.79 %.

description: This protocol describes four different steps: (1) preparation of a custom-made bacterial culture medium kit; (2) cultivation of intestinal commensals in a single medium under anaerobic conditions; (3) preparation of the bacterial mix for intragastric gavage into germ-free (GF) mice; and (4) evaluation of colonization success in these mice. The following protocol involves the use of 14 different, fully sequenced, human gut commensal species, which were previously used to address the role of microbiome-mediated mucus degradation during enteropathogenic infection in a gnotobiotic mouse model (Desai et al., 2016). We have further optimized the growth conditions of the 14 strains in this protocol. Table 1 summarizes the microbial species used in this protocol and Figure 1 illustrates their broad-level phylogenetic relation. Importantly, all of these strains are available from commercial bacterial collections. However, other strains not mentioned in this list can potentially be used instead of the herein listed strains, or in addition to them, depending on specific research interests and after verification of their ability to grow in the recommended bacterial culture medium. The modified yeast- and short-chain fatty acid-containing culture medium (mYCFA) is based on a protocol previously published by Browne et al. (Browne et al., 2016) and its composition was adapted to the needs of the bacterial strains used in this protocol. Thus, as compared to the original protocol, mYCFA does not contain maltose and cellulose. Additionally, mYCFA is supplemented with N-acetyl-D-glucosamine to support growth of the mucin-specialist Akkermansia muciniphila. Furthermore, the concentration of sulfate ions is increased 46-fold and sodium lactate is added to support proper culturability of Desulfovibrio piger.
